title: Algorithmic overlaps in the Baxter-Wu model: cluster dynamics under Novotny-Evertz updates
abstract: We study the spatial overlap of successive spin configurations generated by Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations of the Baxter-Wu model. Using the Novotny-Evertz sublattice-freezing single-cluster update, we track the mean and variance of the algorithmic overlap across the critical region. We show that, even in this three-spin model, the overlap acts as an algorithmic observable that follows the thermodynamics of the transition: the single-cluster overlap mean behaves like an order parameter, dropping from a finite ordered-phase plateau toward zero across $T_c$. The overlap does not diverge at criticality, instead it remains finite and its finite-size value decays as a clean power law, $U_2(T_c)\sim L^{-ψ}$, over eleven sizes with an exponent $ψ{=}0.378(4)$ smaller than the value $\approx0.42$ found for the Ising and Potts models under standard Fortuin-Kasteleyn cluster dynamics, indicating that it reflects the Novotny-Evertz sublattice-freezing dynamics rather than any static property of the model.
summary: The paper analyzes the Baxter-Wu model using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations to study an 'algorithmic overlap' observable. By comparing its critical behavior to established models, the authors demonstrate that this overlap exponent is determined by the specific Novotny-Evertz cluster update rule rather than the model's static universality class. This highlights the diagnostic power of tracking dynamic process metrics in phase transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates whether an 'algorithmic observable' derived from Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations can characterize the thermodynamics of a phase transition in a multi-spin interaction model.
main_result: The algorithmic overlap mean behaves like an order parameter, dropping to zero at $T_c$, but its finite-size decay exponent ($\psi = 0.378(4)$) is smaller than that found for standard cluster dynamics (Ising/Potts), indicating it reflects the specific update rule.
method: The authors simulate the Baxter-Wu model using a specialized Novotny-Evertz sublattice-freezing single-cluster update and measure the spatial overlap between successive spin configurations.
model_or_system: The system is the 2D Baxter–Wu model on the triangular lattice with three-spin interactions ($\mathcal{H}_{	ext{BW}}$). The dynamics are governed by the Novotny–Evertz sublattice-freezing single-cluster update, which differs fundamentally from standard Fortuin–Kasteleyn cluster rules.
key_observables: Algorithmic overlap ($U^{(W)}_n$), its mean $\langle U^{(W)}_n angle$, and its finite-size scaling exponent ($\psi(W)$).
important_parameters: Critical temperature ($T_c$); system size $L$; the measured exponent $\psi = 0.378(4)$.
main_assumptions: The overlap is treated as an algorithmic observable, and its behavior is assumed to be dictated by the specific cluster update rule (NE) rather than static equilibrium properties.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but comparisons are made between $\psi(W)$ for Baxter-Wu (NE dynamics) versus Ising/Potts models (FK dynamics).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the model and the algorithmic observable. It then details the simulation methodology using NE updates. The core of the work presents the measurement of the overlap's behavior across $T_c$ and compares the resulting critical exponent $\psi(W)$ to known results, concluding that the update rule dictates this exponent.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous example of how non-equilibrium or algorithmic observables can serve as powerful diagnostics in statistical mechanics, potentially revealing details about the dynamics inaccessible through standard equilibrium critical exponents.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Three-sublattice coloring of the triangular lattice (A red, B green, C blue); every elementary triangle (gold) has one site of each. The unique three-coloring closes on the torus only when L mod 3=0. This structure underlies both the four-fold degeneracy and the Novotny–Evertz cluster update.

FIG. 2: Baxter–Wu, single-cluster updates. (a) Mean overlap U (W) 2 versus T for L=129–1023. The ordered-phase plateau at ≈0.44 reflects the 2N/3 active spins [Eq. (7)]. (b) Mean overlap versus energy per spin. Inset zooms on the critical region. (c) Energy per spin versus T. The monotonic relation justifies the energy axis in panel (b).

FIG. 3: Finite-size scaling of U (W) 2 (Tc) versus L (log–log) for eleven sizes L=129–1023, with jackknife errors from ∼400 independent replicas; the line is a pure power law A L−ψ with ψ(W) BW =0.378(4) (reduced χ2 ≈0.6), more moderate than the Ising/Potts value.

FIG. 4: (a) Variance Var(U (W) 2 ) versus T; inset on the critical peak. The peak sharpens with L; the low-T plateau is 2/81. (b) Rescaled variance T −2Var(U (W) 2 ) versus C (log–log). Upper branch T < Tc, lower branch T > Tc; they meet at the specific-heat peak.
FIG. 5: U (W) 2 versus (T −Tc)/T; the overlap behaves like an order parameter, dropping from a finite plateau to zero without diverging.
